seoTitle: Motril cruise port guide: shuttle, Granada and Alhambra
seoDescription: Motril cruise ships berth at the Dique quay, 2.5 km from town; shuttles run in. Granada is 45–60 min by road. Alhambra €21 (2026): book ahead, carry ID.
quickAnswer: Ships berth alongside at the Dique quay in the Port of Motril, about 2.5 km from the town centre; there is no cruise terminal building, and shuttle buses carry passengers into Motril. Granada and the Alhambra are 45–60 minutes away by road, or 50–75 minutes on the ALSA bus from Motril. If you go to Granada on your own, leave the Alhambra at least 3 h 45 min before all-aboard by public transport, or leave Granada at least 2 h 30 min before by taxi or private car.
intro: Motril is a working cargo, fishing and ferry port on the Costa Tropical, and most cruise passengers use it as the door to Granada. The Alhambra is the reason to come, but it needs a pre-booked, named ticket with a fixed time for the Nasrid Palaces, and the round trip by road takes up a big part of a port day. The alternative is a slow day in Motril itself: an old centre with a 16th-century church and sugar-cane heritage, fish restaurants on Playa de Poniente, and Salobreña's hilltop old town a short taxi ride west. Calls have grown fast, with 68 ship calls expected in 2026, and Norwegian Dawn calls weekly in summer.

terminals.name: Muelle Dique (Dique quay)
terminals.notes: Cruise ships including the 326 m Norwegian Getaway have berthed here. There is no cruise terminal yet: a large terminal project was dropped and a smaller passenger services building on the bulk quay is only at application stage (2026). Distance to town is quoted as 2.5 km by the regional tourist board and about 4 km by other guides, depending on where in town you measure to.

walkability.detail: The berth sits inside a working cargo port and the town is 2.5–4 km away by road. Use the shuttle bus, which on busy days runs a fleet of eight to ten buses.

transportSections.mode: Port shuttle bus to Motril centre
transportSections.cost: Free on recent calls; confirm on your daily programme (2026)
transportSections.detail: The port and Motril council set up a free town shuttle for cruise passengers, and eight to ten shuttle buses ran on big-ship days in 2024. It goes to the commercial and historic centre. Check the last shuttle time before you leave the ship.

transportSections.cost: Check the fare on alsa.com before travelling (2026)
transportSections.detail: ALSA runs frequent direct buses between Motril and Granada bus station, with the fastest taking about 50 minutes. Granada bus station is outside the centre: take city bus 33 to Catedral, then the C30 minibus up to the Alhambra, about 35 minutes in all. Check the return timetable before you set off and pick a bus with slack.

transportSections.mode: Granada city bus and Alhambra minibus
transportSections.detail: The C30 runs from Calle Pavaneras by Plaza Isabel la Católica up to the Alhambra; the C32 links the Alhambra and the Albaicín about every 10 minutes. A ticket allows a change of line within one hour.

transportSections.mode: Ship excursion or pre-booked private transfer to Granada
transportSections.detail: A motorway links the coast and Granada. The ship's tour waits for its own coaches, which removes the timetable risk on the way back.

returnTiming.rule: From Motril centre, be on a shuttle back 75 minutes before all-aboard. From Granada by public transport, leave the Alhambra 3 h 45 min (225 minutes) before all-aboard; by taxi or private car, leave Granada 2 h 30 min (150 minutes) before.
returnTiming.detail: The Granada return chains three legs: Alhambra minibus and city bus to the bus station (about 35 minutes), the ALSA bus to Motril (50–75 minutes), and a taxi or shuttle to the berth. A missed connection at any point costs time, and summer traffic on the coast road adds more. Aim to be back on board 90 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If an ALSA bus is full or late, take a taxi from Granada straight to the Port of Motril (45–60 minutes). Call the port agent number on your daily programme as soon as you think you may be late.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner

diyVsExcursion.item: Granada city bus and C30 minibus

excursionAdvice: For the Alhambra, the ship's tour is worth considering here. Tickets are named, have a fixed Nasrid Palaces time, sell out weeks ahead, and cannot be changed, and the DIY route needs three connections each way. A ship tour holds the tickets and guarantees the return. Go independently only on a long call, with tickets already booked and the ALSA return timetable checked. For Motril, the beach or Salobreña, you do not need a tour.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30, with a DIY day in Granada and Alhambra tickets booked for a Nasrid Palaces slot around 11:30.

steps.what: Off the ship. Shuttle or taxi into Motril and on to the ALSA bus stop.
ALSA bus to Granada (about 50–75 minutes). Check today's return times before you board.
At Granada bus station take bus 33 to Catedral, then the C30 from Calle Pavaneras up to the Alhambra.
Enter the Alhambra with your passport. See the Alcazaba first.
Nasrid Palaces at the time on your ticket. Be at the entrance early; late arrivals are not let in.
Generalife gardens and the Partal. Eat a packed lunch or buy a snack; there is no time for a sit-down meal.
Leave the Alhambra on the C30, change to bus 33 for the bus station.
ALSA bus back to Motril, then taxi or shuttle to the berth.
Back on board, 90 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Alhambra and Generalife, Granada
sights.why: The Nasrid palaces, the Alcazaba fortress and the Generalife gardens; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sights.timeNeeded: 3 hours inside, plus 2–2.5 hours' travel each way door to door by public transport
sights.cost: €21 General ticket at the ticket office, €22.27 online (2026); gardens-only ticket €12
sights.tip: Book on the official site only; tickets are named and you must show the passport whose number is on the ticket. Open 08:30–20:00 from 1 April to 14 October and 08:30–18:00 from 15 October to 31 March.

sights.name: Albaicín and Mirador de San Nicolás, Granada
sights.why: The old Moorish quarter facing the Alhambra, with the best-known view of it.
sights.tip: Only fits a long call after the Alhambra; the C32 links the two.

sights.name: Alcaicería, Granada
sights.why: The former silk bazaar beside the cathedral, now lanes of shops selling ceramics, lamps and spices.
sights.tip: On the way between the Alhambra minibus and bus 33 at Catedral.

sights.name: Iglesia Mayor de la Encarnación, Motril
sights.why: Motril's oldest monument, begun in 1502 on the site of an old mosque.
sights.tip: In the historic centre near the town hall.

sights.name: Casa de la Palma (Museo Preindustrial de la Caña de Azúcar), Motril
sights.why: The last surviving 16th-century sugar mill in Motril, explaining the town's sugar-cane history.
sights.tip: Ask at the tourist office for opening times on your day.

sights.name: Motril Town Hall and historic centre
sights.why: A 1631 town hall with Mudéjar ceilings, and the pedestrian shopping streets around it.

sights.name: Salobreña
sights.why: A white hilltop town with a castle and views over the coast.
sights.tip: About 8 km west of Motril by taxi; a good half-day if you skip Granada.

beaches.name: Playa de Poniente
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi or shuttle and a short walk
beaches.note: Calm water close to town, with beach restaurants such as Bambú Beach and La Ballena Azul.

beaches.name: Playa Granada
beaches.note: Long beach next to the Los Moriscos golf course.

beaches.name: Calahonda
beaches.note: Known for fishing and water sports; agree the taxi fare first.

La Ballena Azul, Playa de Poniente, Motril

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up in Granada hoping to buy Alhambra tickets on the day.
commonMistakes.fix: Book on the official site, ideally a month ahead. Tickets sell out and cannot be changed or refunded.

commonMistakes.mistake: Booking the Nasrid Palaces slot too late in the day.
commonMistakes.fix: Choose a slot around 11:00–11:30 so you can leave the Alhambra by 13:45 for a 17:30 all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the passport on the ship.
commonMistakes.fix: Alhambra tickets are named; bring the ID whose number you gave when booking.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming Granada's bus station is next to the Alhambra.
commonMistakes.fix: It is outside the centre. Allow about 35 minutes by bus 33 and the C30 minibus each way.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying cheap Alhambra tickets from a reseller.
commonMistakes.fix: Only the official Alhambra ticket site sells the €21–22.27 ticket. Cheaper offers may cover only the gardens or nothing at all.

safety: Motril and Granada are generally safe. Inside the cargo port, follow the marked route and use the shuttle instead of walking among lorries and port machinery. In Granada watch your bags on crowded minibuses and around the Alhambra and Albaicín viewpoints. Summer heat inland is strong; carry water and shade for the Alhambra gardens.
scams: Unofficial Alhambra ticket sites: sites offering tickets below the official price may sell only gardens access, an expensive tour or nothing at all. Buy only on the official Alhambra ticket site.
'Guided tours' around €30 that include nothing more than the standard entry ticket, or only the audioguide the official site provides free.
accessibility: Ships berth alongside, so no tender transfer is needed. Ask the ship whether the shuttle buses are accessible before you leave. In Granada, the Alhambra minibuses are small and the Alhambra itself has long distances, slopes and some steps; parts of the Nasrid Palaces and Generalife are uneven. The Albaicín is steep and cobbled. Motril's centre and the Playa de Poniente promenade are flatter options.
rainyDay: Rain does not close the Alhambra, but the gardens and Alcazaba walls are exposed, so bring waterproofs. In Motril, the sugar-cane museum at Casa de la Palma, the Encarnación church and a long lunch in town make a short wet-weather day.
crowdTips: The Alhambra controls numbers with fixed Nasrid Palaces slots, so the main crowd risk is not getting a ticket at all. Book early. In Motril, the first shuttles fill with everyone heading to town; ship tours leave first, so independent passengers can take a later shuttle without a queue. On big-ship days several thousand passengers share eight to ten shuttles.

faqs.a: Usually not. Cruise ships berth alongside at the Dique quay; anchorage and tendering are possible but not normal.

faqs.q: Is Motril walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: No. The town centre is 2.5–4 km away through a working port; use the shuttle bus.

faqs.q: How far is Granada from Motril cruise port?
faqs.a: About 65–70 km, or 45–60 minutes by road. The ALSA bus takes about 50–75 minutes to Granada bus station.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Alhambra on my own from Motril?
faqs.a: Yes on a long call, with a pre-booked named ticket and a Nasrid Palaces slot around 11:00–11:30. Leave the Alhambra 3 h 45 min before all-aboard by bus.

faqs.q: How much is the Alhambra ticket?
faqs.a: The General ticket is €21 at the ticket office or €22.27 online (2026). The gardens, Generalife, Partal and Alcazaba ticket is €12.

faqs.q: What can I do in Motril in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Granada and the Alhambra, or a slower day in Motril's old centre, Playa de Poniente and Salobreña.
Playa de Poniente is close to town with calm water; Playa Granada and Calahonda are short taxi rides along the coast.
Yes. Use the shuttle rather than walking through the cargo port, and watch bags on Granada's busy minibuses.
